Security review of the Tauri desktop app implementation. Read and review these files for authentication gaps, input validation/sanitization, hardcoded secrets, injection vulnerabilities, and attack surface:

Python backend:
- /home/dev/src/transcribe/src/web/app.py (shutdown secret, feeder token, host allowlist, origin check, moonshine endpoint, traversal rejection)
- /home/dev/src/transcribe/src/live/session.py (TAURI_EVENT stdout emission)
- /home/dev/src/transcribe/src/live/moonshine_fetch.py (license gate)
- /home/dev/src/transcribe/src/ffmpeg_patch.py (subprocess patching)
- /home/dev/src/transcribe/main.py (dynamic port binding)

Rust shell:
- /home/dev/src/transcribe/src-tauri/src/process.rs (spawn, env injection, shutdown secret generation)
- /home/dev/src/transcribe/src-tauri/src/downloader.rs (zip extraction, path traversal, manifest validation)
- /home/dev/src/transcribe/src-tauri/src/webview.rs (navigation policy, permission handler)
- /home/dev/src/transcribe/src-tauri/src/capture.rs (WS feeder auth)
- /home/dev/src/transcribe/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json (CSP, capabilities)
- /home/dev/src/transcribe/src-tauri/capabilities/default.json

Focus on: shutdown secret comparison (timing-safe?), feeder token validation, zip-slip protection, DNS rebinding defense, CSP adequacy, WebView2 permission scope, env var injection, HF token storage. Do NOT run builds or tests. Static review only. Write your findings to /tmp/security-review.md with items tagged [critical/major/minor/info] and a summary at the top.

validationOutput: No [critical] findings. 3 [major], 7 [minor], 7 [info]. Highest-value fix: add CSP + X-Frame-Options + nosniff middleware to the FastAPI backend (src/web/app.py). Second: strip TRANSCRIBE_SHUTDOWN_SECRET/HF_TOKEN from spawned subprocess env in ffmpeg_patch.py. Third: move bootstrap JS external so script-src 'self' can replace 'unsafe-inline'.
residualRisks: Entire Rust shell is 【未検証】 (never compiled/run on Windows): security policies are correct on paper but COM/windows-rs/cpal wiring must be confirmed at first Windows build.
Runtime-download integrity relies on bundled manifest + installer code-signing / resource-dir ACLs, not on an in-app trust anchor.
Backend HTTP origin has no CSP/framing headers until the [major] finding is addressed.
Shutdown-secret leak to ffmpeg env is a defense-in-depth gap, not a confirmed exploit (ffmpeg is bundled/trusted).

reviewFindings: major: src/web/app.py — no CSP / X-Frame-Options / frame-ancestors / nosniff on the backend HTTP origin (only the bootstrap tauri origin is CSP'd); dashboard is frameable and any future template XSS is uncontained

major: src-tauri/tauri.conf.json + src-tauri/bootstrap/index.html — script-src 'unsafe-inline' with withGlobalTauri:true gives any bootstrap XSS full IPC access (save_hf_token/start_backend/open_external); status() uses innerHTML with invoke-error strings
major: src-tauri/src/process.rs + src/ffmpeg_patch.py — TRANSCRIBE_SHUTDOWN_SECRET (also the feeder token) is inherited by ffmpeg and all sidecar subprocesses via the env block
minor: src/web/app.py live_ws — feeder (no-Origin) WS connections accepted with no token when TRANSCRIBE_SHUTDOWN_SECRET is unset (dev-only path)
minor: src/web/app.py moonshine_status — GET /internal/models/moonshine exposes download status without the x-transcribe-internal gate that the POST has
minor: src/web/templates/detail.html — {{ structure|tojson }}/{{ graph|tojson }} in <script> rely on Jinja2>=3.1 HTML-safe tojson; pin the version
minor: src-tauri/src/downloader.rs read_manifest — url+sha256 come from the same bundled manifest; trust root is installer signing/ACLs, not the in-app check
minor: src-tauri/src/downloader.rs extract_zip — symlink zip entries not explicitly rejected; potential zip-slip-via-symlink depending on zip-crate behavior; confirm and reject symlink entries

minor: src-tauri/src/process.rs build_env_block — inherits entire parent env; a pre-existing HF_TOKEN leaks to the sidecar even with no keyring token; HTTPS_PROXY honored by downloader (documented trade-off, SHA-256 still guards integrity)
info: src/web/app.py — shutdown/feeder token comparison uses hmac.compare_digest (timing-safe); secret is OsRng 32-byte; positive control
info: src/web/app.py — Host allowlist applied to all HTTP + WS handshake; WEB_HOST pinned to 127.0.0.1 by Rust shell; DNS-rebinding defense OK
info: src/live/session.py — TAURI_EVENT payload contains only hardcoded capture value + generated session_id; no untrusted input on stdout command channel
info: src-tauri/src/webview.rs — WebView2 permission handler grants microphone-only for exact backend origin, denies all else; policy correct (wiring 【未検証】)
info: src-tauri/capabilities/default.json — no dangerousRemoteDomainIpcAccess; remote backend origin gets no Tauri IPC; positive control
info: src-tauri/tauri.conf.json — updater ships placeholder endpoint+pubkey and createUpdaterArtifacts:false; remove the plugins.updater block until a real key/endpoint exist
childReport.manualNotes: Static review only; no builds or tests run per task instructions. Several Rust modules self-mark as 【未検証】 (never compiled on Windows) — the security policies reviewed are correct but the native API wiring was not and cannot be verified without a Windows toolchain. Recommendation priorities: (1) backend CSP+framing headers, (2) strip secrets from child env, (3) external bootstrap JS, (4) reject zip symlink entries, (5) allow-list sidecar env.
